title: A covered call is a transfer of risk, not rent on your shares
summary: The speaker rejects the idea that covered calls are like renting out an apartment. A landlord keeps the gain if the building triples in value. A covered call writer's gain stops at the strike. Selling calls is an active transfer of risk: you sell future upside for payment today.

steps.caption: The stock trades at $100. Compare the shares alone with the shares plus a $110 call.
Line A: the owner keeps all upside, like a landlord whose building rises in value.
Line B: the covered call. Its gain stops at $110 plus the premium.
The gap above $110 is the upside you sold. If the stock triples, it is most of the gain.
Below the strike, the premium gives only a small cushion. The downside stays with you.

takeaways: Covered calls are not rent: a landlord keeps the property's gains, a call writer does not.
Selling a call transfers upside risk to the buyer for a premium today.
This view should drive how you choose strikes, underlyings and when to use the strategy.
caveats: The 'triples in value' case is an illustration from the speaker, not a forecast.
